title: What You Can Bring Into Türkiye: Customs Allowances and a Packing Check
excerpt: Cigarettes, alcohol, gifts, food, phones and medicines: the current per-person customs allowances for travellers arriving in Türkiye, how the €430 gift limit works after the Ministry of Trade's November 2026 clarification, and why other websites quote different numbers.

body.text: Most visitors walk through Turkish customs without stopping, and that is how it should be. The questions start when your bag holds something beyond clothes and a toothbrush: gifts for friends, a second phone, a carton of cigarettes, a bottle from the airport shop, spices or cheese from home. In early November 2026 the Ministry of Trade restated how the €430 passenger exemption works, as [Türkiye Today reported on 2 November](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/nation/turkiye-clarifies-430-customs-exemption-for-travelers-what-is-excluded-3231551). This guide turns the current official allowances into a packing check you can run before you fly, and explains why you will find different numbers on other websites.
Which source to trust when numbers disagree

Customs rules for passengers come from Customs Law No. 4458 and a government decision on passenger exemptions; the Ministry of Trade administers them and publishes a [passenger transactions FAQ](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri/sikca-sorulan-sorular/english/passenger-transactions) in English, including the personal-goods list known as Appendix-9. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs repeats the same core figures on its [information page on Turkish customs](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/turkiye_ye-ait-gumruk-bilgileri.en.mfa). An older [duty-free goods page on the Culture and Tourism Ministry site](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/EN-120416/duty-free-goods.html) still lists earlier figures — 200 cigarettes, one or two bottles of wine or spirits, 1.5 kg of coffee — alongside items such as a portable typewriter and a pocket PC with 128 MB of RAM, which shows its age, yet figures like these still circulate on many travel sites. Where the pages differ, this guide follows the Ministry of Trade text; check that page again shortly before you travel, because allowances can change and customs officers make the final assessment at the border.
Tobacco and alcohol: the per-person limits
According to the Ministry of Trade FAQ, each passenger aged 18 or over may bring in, free of duty and as accompanied baggage:

items: 600 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos (up to 3 g each), or 50 cigars, or 250 g of shredded tobacco with 200 papers, or 250 g of pipe tobacco;
1 litre of an alcoholic drink stronger than 22%, or 2 litres of a drink of 22% or less;
nothing at all if you are under 18 — the tobacco and alcohol allowance does not apply to minors;
these goods cannot be sent ahead by post or express cargo; they must travel with you.

body.text: The Foreign Affairs page adds that each product can be used separately within its own limit. The allowances are per passenger, so count them for each adult in your group rather than for the family as a whole.
Gifts and other goods: what the €430 covers

Beyond the listed personal items, gifts and other goods that are not for trade are exempt up to a combined value of €430 per passenger, or €150 for passengers under 15. Your clothing for personal use is assessed separately and does not count toward this total, according to the November clarification. Values are taken from your invoice or receipt; if there is none, or it looks low, customs sets the value.

If you go over, only the part up to the limit is exempt. For passengers over 18, the excess on goods worth up to €1,500 is charged at a single flat rate: 30% for goods coming directly from an EU country and 60% from elsewhere; the Foreign Affairs page adds a further 20% for some specially listed goods. Above €1,500, normal import duty rates apply. Anything in commercial quantity does not qualify at all.

items: Tea, coffee, instant coffee, chocolate and sugar-based sweets: 1 kg each. The Foreign Affairs page notes you may use the full 2 kg for either chocolate or sugar-based food.
Plant-based food: the Trade FAQ gives a single 3 kg limit; the Foreign Affairs page allows up to 3 kg of fresh or dried fruit and vegetables and up to 1 kg of other plant products.
Meat, dairy and other animal products: not allowed, whether carried or posted. Leave the cheese and sausage at home.

Perfume, cologne and lotions: the Trade FAQ lists five bottles of up to 120 ml each; the Foreign Affairs page describes it as up to 600 ml in total plus up to five skincare or make-up products. Either way, normal holiday quantities are fine.

body.text: Your own laptop, camera, video camera, games console and one mobile phone are personal goods. The Foreign Affairs page says valuable items may need to be declared so customs can confirm on departure that you are taking them out again; personal travel goods cannot be left in the country. Phones are the special case: the Trade FAQ allows one phone per passenger every three calendar years, and phones cannot come in as gifts, by post or by paying duty. Using a phone bought abroad with a Turkish SIM card requires registering the device and paying a fee first; the Foreign Affairs page gives TRY 45,614.20 "as of 2025". Check the current amount through official channels before you plan on a local line for a foreign handset.

Medicines for your own use are allowed in reasonable quantities if you can show the doctor's report or prescription to customs, according to both ministries; the Foreign Affairs page adds that the acceptable quantity depends on the length of your stay. Keep them in their original packaging and carry the paperwork in your hand luggage. Up to two pets (cats, dogs or birds) or ten aquarium fish may travel with you, with a veterinary health report, vaccination and origin documents and identity documents; they are checked by a veterinarian on arrival.

Use the green lane only if everything you carry is within the allowances, not for trade, and not prohibited or restricted. If you are over a limit, carrying something you are unsure about, or bringing a valuable item you want registered, use the red lane and declare it. The Foreign Affairs page warns that exceeding allowances or carrying prohibited items can lead to fines or worse; declaring costs a few minutes.

items: Count cigarettes and bottles per adult, not per family; leave tobacco and alcohol out of children's bags.
Add up the value of gifts (not your clothes) and keep the receipts; aim to stay under €430 per traveller aged 15 or over, or €150 per child under 15.
Remove meat, cheese and other animal products.
Put medicines in original packs with the prescription or doctor's report.
Decide whether any expensive camera, laptop or jewellery should be declared on arrival so departure is simple.
If you plan to use a Turkish SIM in a phone bought abroad for a long stay, check the current registration fee first.

Need a wider plan for your first days? See our notes on [staying safe and avoiding common scams](/blog/turkey-tourist-scams-how-to-avoid), and our [7-day itinerary for Istanbul and Cappadocia](/blog/7-day-turkey-itinerary-istanbul-cappadocia).

body.text: This guide covers what you bring into Türkiye. Rules for taking things out — antiques, older carpets and historical objects in particular — are separate, and we have not covered them here because the official guidance could not be verified for this article. If you plan such a purchase, ask the seller for the documents customs will expect before you pay. For trip-specific questions, [get in touch with our team](/contact).

seo.intent: Traveller wants to know what goods, gifts, tobacco, alcohol, food, phones and medicines they can bring into Türkiye without paying duty, and when to declare.
keywords: what can I bring into Turkey
seo.uniqueValue: Reconciles the current Ministry of Trade and Foreign Affairs allowance figures with the outdated list still widely copied, applies the November 2026 €430 clarification, and turns it into a per-person packing check.

quality.reviewNotes: Independent review 2026-11-14 (separate agent opened all four sources: ticaret.gov.tr passenger FAQ, mfa.gov.tr customs page, ktb.gov.tr duty-free page, Türkiye Today 2026-11-02). All tobacco/alcohol, €430/€150, 30%/60% up to €1,500, food, perfume (Trade vs MFA discrepancy shown), electronics, one phone per three years, TRY 45,614.20 'as of 2025', medicines and pets figures confirmed against Trade and MFA. Fixes applied in all five locales after review: KTB alcohol wording ('one or two bottles'), plant-food limits attributed (Trade 3 kg vs MFA 3 kg/1 kg), €430 'per traveller aged 15 or over', phone registration tied to Turkish SIM use without unsourced duration/annual-revision claims, Ministry of Trade 'administers and publishes' rather than 'sets', added 'allowances can change; customs makes the final assessment' and MFA's length-of-stay note for medicines. Reviewer pre-fix score 84; 87 after fixes. Risk judged low: attributed travel-logistics information, no individual legal, medical or financial advice. Export rules (antiques, carpets) and cash thresholds deliberately not covered: ktb.gov.tr customs guide blocked by robots.txt. Note: the approved-primary-domain list contains ktb.gov.tr but not ticaret.gov.tr or mfa.gov.tr, which are the authoritative sources here. Translations DE/zh-CN/KO/ES reviewed block by block: no omissions, number changes or material errors; English-only link targets labelled.
